# dsh-model-proxy
English | 中文

Route DeepSeek Harness **model API requests** through a proxy so third-party overseas
model provider

s work from mainland China, while **requests outside the domains you list stay
direct** — web search

, page fetching, MCP servers and tool calls are not proxied unless you
add their domains.

- Does not patch any harness file; uninstalling restores the original behaviour exactly
- **System p
roxy**, **custom proxy** (`http` / `https` / `socks4` / `socks4a` / `socks5` / `socks5h`), or env-ba

sed
- **Global** or **per-domain** routing; domain rules accept exact hosts, wildcards and suffixes
- Three safety guarantees that configuration cannot loosen (below)
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart DSH afterwards — the host half loads inside the harness process.

Requires **DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 or newer** and **Node 22.19+** (the floor the harness itself
declares in `

engines`). The settings page is generated by the host from the
plugin's `Config` schema (`0.2.x` rem

oved the `settings` service and the client-side
`settingsScope` service), so older harnesses are rej
ected at install time.
### Upgrading from 1.x

Nothing to do by hand: on first start after the upgrade the plugin converts old settings
in memory a

nd says so on the settings page. Two conversions matter — `enabled: false`
becomes `mode: 'off'` (so

a proxy you had turned off does not silently come back), and a
comma-separated domain list becomes

a proper list. Press **Save** once when the page asks;
otherwise the conversion is redone, visibly,

Press **Save** once when the page asks;
otherwise the conversion is redone, visibly, on every start.
## Configure
Open **Settings — Model Proxy** (its own page in the settings sidebar).
| Field | Meaning |

| Mode | `rule` (recommended) / `system` / `custom` / `off` |
| Proxy protocol | http / https / sock

s5 / socks5h / socks4 |
| Proxy address | `socks5h://127.0.0.1:7890`, or just `127.0.0.1:7890` (sche

me filled in from the protocol field) |
| Proxy only these domains | empty = built-in preset; otherw
ise one entry per chip (`*.openai.com`, `.aiplatform.googleapis.com`), added with Enter or **Add** |
| Exclude domains | always direct, highest priority (same chip editor) |
Changes take effect on the next request — no restart.
### Three common setups

**A. Clash / V2Ray on `127.0.0.1:7890`, overseas APIs only**
Mode = `rule`, protocol = `http`, addre

ss = `127.0.0.1:7890`, leave the domain list empty.
The preset sends OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / x

AI / Groq / OpenRouter and similar through
the proxy, and keeps DeepSeek, DashScope, Zhipu, Kimi and
other mainland providers direct.

**B. Follow the Windows system proxy**
Mode = `system`. The plugin re-reads
`HKCU\Software\Microsoft

\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings` every 30 s and follows
changes made in Windows.

**C. Everything through the proxy, a few exceptions**
Mode = `custom`, fill the address, list the ex
ceptions under "Exclude domains".
### Notes for overseas APIs from mainland China

- **DNS poisoning**: prefer `socks5h` (DNS resolved by the proxy), or let your proxy client
take ove

r DNS.
- **Plaintext `http` is refused by default** — an API key must not travel over a proxy in
cle

ar text. Tick the option on the settings page if you really need it.
- The proxy must listen on loop
back; enable the local/LAN listener in your proxy client.
## Verify

1. The settings page shows live status: `path A · exit route · N rules · proxied x / direct y`.
2. `

http://127.0.0.1:<port>/dsh-model-proxy/status` returns the same snapshot as JSON
(loopback / same-o

rigin only).
3. In a source checkout: `npm test` (= `node test/run-all.mjs`). The suite ships with t

he
repository, not with the npm package, and needs no install — it resolves the host's own
`undici`
and `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` from your DSH profile (or `DSH_HOME`).
## Safety guarantees
These hold regardless of configuration, and are what the rules engine checks first:

c00::/7` — `localhost` and `.local`/`.lan`/`.internal` style names never go
through a proxy. User ru

les can add entries but cannot remove these.
2. **Plaintext gate** — a model request that is not `ht

tps` is rejected before any socket is
opened, unless the option is explicitly enabled (the page then

shows a standing warning).
3. **Data minimisation** — the plugin passes request and response bodies

through as streams;
it never parses them, never writes them to disk, and never reads `Authorization

` or any
provider API key. Default logging records the exit id and error class only — no hostnames,
no paths, no bodies.

A failed exit falls back to **direct**, never to another exit: silently moving traffic to a
differen

t exit would change the outbound identity without the user noticing. The fallback is
logged and show
n on the settings page, so a degraded state is visible rather than silent.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`undici` and `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` are both **peers** — the harness already ships them,
and ins

talling a second copy would mean two dispatcher/`Schema` instances. The `devDependencies`
[该节后续省略]
## Limitations

- Covers requests issued through **`fetch`** — in practice every model request, plus any
other `fetc

h` traffic whose domain you add to the proxy list. `transport: websocket` streaming
and provider nat

ive-SDK channels (e.g. Amazon Bedrock) do not pass through `fetch` and cannot be
proxied here — use

the harness's built-in environment-variable proxy for those. Web page
fetching is in the same catego

ry: the harness's fetch tool builds its own `undici` agent, so
domain rules never see it.
- Routing

is by **domain**. A domain that serves both a model API and other traffic sends all
of it through th

e proxy; list such domains under "Exclude domains".
- Proxy credentials can only be embedded in the

proxy address (`http://user:pass@host:port`),
which stores them in plain text in settings. Prefer le

tting the proxy accept loopback
connections without authentication.
- Proxy **chains** are supported

to any depth (each hop's CONNECT is relayed through the previous
one, in configuration order). Ever

y hop is a real hop: the chain test suite drives three
CONNECT stubs and asserts which port each one

a real hop: the chain test suite drives three
CONNECT stubs and asserts which port each one dialled.
